**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

The licence grant to AbbVie satisfies the preferred playbook position on all three material terms:

- **Affiliates/contractors:** § 5.3 permits sublicensing through multiple tiers to "its Affiliates and other Persons" without consent (copy delivered post-execution only), reinforced by § 5.4 (distributors), § 5.5 (co-promotion with Third Parties) and § 13.16 (performance by Affiliates).
- **Not revocable at will:** Harpoon has no convenience-termination right; termination is confined to uncured material breach (§ 12.2, 90-day cure plus a last-resort limitation) and insolvency (§ 12.4). § 5.1.3(c) makes the grants automatically effective, and § 12.1.2 converts them to non-exclusive, fully-paid, royalty-free and **irrevocable** on expiry. § 12.3 gives us a unilateral at-will termination right — in our favour, so not flagged.
- **Transferability:** § 13.4.1 allows assignment without consent to an Affiliate or to a successor by merger, stock sale or asset sale, and binds the grant of rights on Harpoon's successors.

Noted only in the rationale (not a deviation): the pre-option grants at §§ 5.1.1–5.1.2 are co-exclusive and purpose-limited, which reflects the option structure of the deal rather than a scope shortfall.
